catalog_quote: Sur le plan suprasegmental, chaque noyau syllabique en nsong porte au moins un ton. Il y a deux tons simples de base qui sont distinctifs lexicalement ainsi que grammaticalement : un ton haut [ ́] et un ton bas (non indiqué). p. ex. édzín ‘dent’ / édzin ‘nom’; lɔ́bá ‘flèche’ / lɔ́ba ‘noix de palme’. Les tons modulés, montant [ˇ] et descendant [ˆ], sont toujours le résultat de contact direct entre deux tons simples : p. ex. bwǎr /bɔ-ár/ ‘habille-toi !’; bwâr /bɔ́-ar/ ‘pirogue’.

new_statements.translation: At the suprasegmental level, every syllable nucleus in Nsong carries at least one tone. There are two basic level tones which are distinctive both lexically and grammatically: a high tone [ ] and a low tone (unmarked). [...] The contour tones, rising and falling, are always the result of direct contact between two level tones.

new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (71 pp., Göteborg Africana Informal Series 6, open Ghent file). Section 2 'La langue nsong' runs pp. 2-7 (PDF 8-13); the quoted passage is at the top of p. 6 (PDF p. 12), verified both in extracted text output and on the rendered page image. Wording is verbatim: 'Sur le plan suprasegmental, chaque noyau syllabique en nsong porte au moins un ton. Il y a deux tons simples de base qui sont distinctifs lexicalement ainsi que grammaticalement : un ton haut [ ́] et un ton bas (non indiqué).. Les tons modulés, montant [ ˇ] et descendant [ ˆ], sont toujours le résultat de contact direct entre deux tons simples'. The only differences are the tone glyphs (acute, caron, circumflex) missing from…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Nsong is described as a two-tone (H/L) language in which every syllable nucleus bears a tone; tone is contrastive lexically and grammatically and contours arise from adjacent level tones. The source says nothing about word stress or accent, so no stress position can be read from it.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the note is a brief sketch. The 2014 ZASPiL paper (p. 127) adds that a focused pronoun 'always carries a high tone', i.e. a tonal, not stress, marking of focus.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level description of the Nsong of the Kikwit villages (southern and northern village groups both surveyed); the sketch precedes a plant-name wordlist. The tone-mark glyphs are missing from the PDF text layer (bracketed blanks in the quote), so the quote's diacritics must be read from the page image.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source describes Nsong proper (Bantu B85d, labelled 'B85F' on its title page), spoken in the villages around Kikwit (Kafumba, Kisala, Kabamba, Mbushi, Makungika in the south; Kiyaka, Kisumba, Mbelo, Bulumbu in the north), not the Mpiin (B863) variety that Glottolog folds into song1299 'Nsong-Mpiin'. Two Glottolog references filed under song1299 describe differently named varieties ('tsong' in Mimpiya 1979 = Nsong; 'pindi' in Yamba-Yamba 1985, identity unverified).

sources.note: Section 2 'La langue nsong' (pp. 2-7) gives vowels (7, ATR harmony, contrastive length), 33 consonants and, p. 6, the suprasegmentals: every syllable nucleus bears at least one tone, two level tones H and L distinctive lexically and grammatically, rising/falling contours only from tone contact. Stress/accent is never mentioned.
